open_points.subject: models M29–M34 value delivery
open_points.text: Like M22–M29 they are the shapes of rows of tables the data provider holds for the release (SPEC_STANDARD §6.10), not reference tables of the specification, which never reach the running service (§5, §15.2).
open_points.question: Do the generated rules read these six release tables, or are their rows design facts that stay outside the generated specification?
options: Generated rules read provider constants for all six tables.
The tables stay outside generated code; State 2 states every required outcome directly.
Only some tables reach generated code, with the text naming which ones.
open_points.default_guess: Generated rules read provider constants for all six tables.

witness.initial: A release contains the M29–M34 tables and a generated operation needs a refusal or transition selected by one of them.
events: The specification generator reads the changed description.
One implementer treats the provider-held table as runtime policy; another treats it as design-only information because the statement that generated code reads it was removed.
outcomes: The operation selects its result from the release table.
The operation hard-codes or independently reconstructs the result without reading the table.
witness.observer: The owner changing a table row in a later release sees whether service behaviour follows that row.

open_points.subject: M29 OwnerFormField
open_points.text: The release: the owner form table the data provider holds.
open_points.question: What imported provider constant must a module note name when generated code reads the owner form table?
options: Use an imported `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` constant.
Choose another explicitly declared imported constant name.
Keep the table outside generated code and do not import it.
consequences: `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` gives later notes a stable symbol and preserves the former naming pattern.
Another declared symbol is behaviourally equivalent but changes generated imports and notes.
Keeping it outside code requires every code-visible form decision to be stated elsewhere; a note cannot refer to this prose as a value source.
open_points.requirement: The release: the owner form table the data provider holds.

open_points.subject: M30 FormFieldRefusalKind
open_points.text: The release: the form refusal table the data provider holds.
open_points.question: What imported provider constant must a module note name when generated code reads the form-refusal correspondence?
options: Use the former imported `FORM_FIELD_REFUSAL_KINDS` constant.
Choose another explicitly declared imported constant name.
Keep the correspondence outside generated code and state both refusal outcomes directly in each consuming rule.
consequences: Restoring `FORM_FIELD_REFUSAL_KINDS` makes the decided correspondence reachable without inventing a symbol.
Another declared symbol works but later generators must choose and consistently emit that different import.
Keeping it outside code prevents table-driven changes and requires consuming rules to carry the complete refusal mapping.
open_points.requirement: The release: the form refusal table the data provider holds.

open_points.subject: M31 ProjectStatusConfirmation
open_points.text: The release: the project confirmation table the data provider holds.
open_points.question: What imported provider constant must a module note name when generated code reads the project-status-to-confirmed-action correspondence?
options: Use the former imported `PROJECT_STATUS_CONFIRMATIONS` constant.
Choose another explicitly declared imported constant name.
Keep the correspondence outside generated code and state each status outcome directly in consuming rules.
consequences: Restoring `PROJECT_STATUS_CONFIRMATIONS` supplies a stable code path for the release table.
Another declared symbol changes imports and notes without changing the required behaviour.
Keeping it outside code requires the active and archived outcomes to be duplicated wherever they are consumed.
open_points.requirement: The release: the project confirmation table the data provider holds.

open_points.subject: M32 ImportFormFailureField
open_points.text: The release: the import form failure table the data provider holds.
open_points.question: What imported provider constant must a module note name when generated code reads the form-field-to-import-mapping-field correspondence?
options: Use the former imported `IMPORT_FORM_FIELD_MAPPING_FIELDS` constant.
Choose another explicitly declared imported constant name.
Keep the correspondence outside generated code and state every failure-field result directly in consuming rules.
consequences: Restoring `IMPORT_FORM_FIELD_MAPPING_FIELDS` makes the release mapping reachable as a provider constant.
Another declared symbol requires a different generated import and note wording.
Keeping it outside code requires a complete duplicated mapping; the examples alone do not provide a value path.
open_points.requirement: The release: the import form failure table the data provider holds.

open_points.subject: M33 CustomerEligibilityRefusal
open_points.text: The release: the customer eligibility refusal table the data provider holds.
open_points.question: What imported provider constant must a module note name when generated code reads the eligibility-to-refusal correspondence?
options: Use the former imported `CUSTOMER_ELIGIBILITY_REFUSALS` constant.
Choose another explicitly declared imported constant name.
Keep the correspondence outside generated code and state each refusal directly in consuming rules.
consequences: Restoring `CUSTOMER_ELIGIBILITY_REFUSALS` makes release-controlled refusal selection reachable.
Another declared symbol preserves outcomes but changes generated imports and notes.
Keeping it outside code requires erased, restricted and ended refusal choices to be carried directly by every consumer.
open_points.requirement: The release: the customer eligibility refusal table the data provider holds.

open_points.subject: M34 StoreCompanionStepSuffix
open_points.text: The release: the store companion table the data provider holds.
open_points.question: What imported provider constant must a module note name when generated code reads the discard-step-to-file-suffix correspondence?
options: Use the former imported `STORE_COMPANION_STEP_SUFFIXES` constant.
Choose another explicitly declared imported constant name.
Keep the correspondence outside generated code and state every exact suffix directly in the installation rule.
consequences: Restoring `STORE_COMPANION_STEP_SUFFIXES` provides the exact release values through a named provider constant.
Another declared symbol changes the generated import and note wording.
Keeping it outside code requires the installation rule to supply the exact suffix strings; descriptive names such as write-ahead log and shared memory are insufficient as code values.
open_points.requirement: The release: the store companion table the data provider holds.
